decision: Originate every R-core new-feature observation from a seed-built binary: build the changed compiler/runtime strictly with the R-seed toolchain under its reviewed bootstrap recipe (go1.27.1 with pinned inputs), run the new-feature corpus on the resulting seed-built bin/canlc, and treat its output as the originating record. The candidate-built binary mirrors that record byte-for-byte and originates nothing. Capabilities outside what the seed-built binary can execute fall back to fixed hand-reviewed vectors with explicit bootstrap bridge assumptions naming the gap.
interpretation: Three fresh phrasings unanimously favor seed_built_oracle (0.98, 1.00, 0.96). Agreement is advisory only; the choice is independently supported by the P06 refresh lane's producer rule (observations must originate from the refresh seed binary, never from candidate compiler C), which fixed_vectors satisfies trivially but at unreviewable-human-bandwidth cost for a 231-file delta, and which dual_build_agreement weakens by letting agreement without an oracle stand as truth. It does not prove correctness or remove bias, and authorizes no execution or qualification.
